newsitem.title: INDIA: Ruling alliance says India PM will not resign. [CORRECTED 21:22 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Ruling alliance says India PM will not resign. [CORRECTED 21:22 GMT]

text.p: India's ruling United Front alliance said on Sunday (corrects from Friday) that Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda will not resign but face parliament when it re-convenes on April 21.

"There is no question of the resignation of Mr Deve Gowda," United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy told reporters after the Congress party, the ruling coalition's meak-or-break ally, said it had withdrawn its support for the nine-month old government

"The decision of the Congress president is unfortunate," Reddy said, referring to Congress chief Sitaram Kesri's meeting with President Shankar Dayal Sharma earlier on Sunday where he demanded Deve Gowda's resignation.

An official at the Presidential Palace said Sharma would seek the views of legal experts before deciding whether to ask Kesri to form a new government or to direct Deve Gowda to face a vote of confidence in parliament.
"If required, the United Front government will face Lok Sabha (lower house of parliament) and we hope the president of India gives the United Front a fair opportunity to do so," Reddy said.
Kesri earlier informed Sharma he was going to formally stake his claim to form a government. Congress officials said Kesri was likely to make his bid on Monday.
